transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I, um... I hope I'm in the right place. It's probably just a bit of normal work stress, honestly, so I don't want to make a bigger deal out of it than it is. 

But... well, I'm an IT systems manager, and lately, what brings me in is that I just keep getting these thoughts. Like, if I miss just one setting, or one access rule, or some small warning sign on the network... someone could get hurt, or people could lose absolutely everything. And I know it sounds a little silly when I say it out loud. Part of me knows it’s irrational. But it just hits me so hard, like I’m personally responsible if the worst happens, and I just can’t seem to move on from it. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Can you tell me more about these thoughts? Specifically, do they keep coming back even when you try not to think about them, and do they cause you a lot of anxiety or discomfort?

Yes, exactly. Um, like I was just saying, it's always that same loop about missing one setting or, you know, one access rule. And... yeah, I really do try to push them away. I promise I do. I tell myself to just stop being silly and focus on my actual work. But they just keep coming back anyway. It’s like my brain literally won't let me move on from it. 

As for the anxiety... I mean, I don't want to sound dramatic, but yes, it does cause a lot of discomfort. It just hits me so hard, this heavy, overwhelming feeling that someone is going to get hurt or lose everything, and it'll be entirely my fault. I know it's irrational, I really do. I hope I don't sound completely crazy admitting all this... am I answering your question okay?

When you have these thoughts, do you feel driven to do certain things over and over — like checking settings repeatedly or going through mental rituals — to try to ease the anxiety or prevent something bad from happening?

Well... yes. You, um, you really hit the nail on the head there. I guess I do have a few... routines. I mean, it's good to be thorough in my line of work, right? You have to be careful. 

But... I suppose I might take it a little further than most people. I really don't want you to think I'm totally out of control, because I still do my job well, I promise. But... I will find myself rereading deployment plans, and audit logs... just over and over. Even silly things, like old emails, or checking the physical door locks at work. 

And you mentioned mental things... sometimes I, um... I count through the steps in my head. I just keep counting them until it finally feels... 'safe.' I know it sounds ridiculous for a grown man to say that. 

It’s just... well, it's gotten to the point where I’ve been staying at the office for hours after everyone else goes home. If I try to just pack up and leave before the checking feels complete, I start to completely panic. I just can't walk away. 

I hope that's not too weird to admit. Am I giving you the right kind of information? I want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms, including recurrent and intrusive thoughts causing significant distress, repetitive behaviors (checking settings, mental rituals), and impairment in functioning, strongly suggest OCD (F42.9). Other disorders like adjustment disorder (F43.2), generalized anxiety (F41.1), or depressive disorders (F32.9, F33.9) may present with overlapping symptoms but are less consistent with the full clinical picture described.
